title: Observability decision rubric & trace experiment notebook
content:
Context: Draft working notebook intended to help the observations team prioritize instrumentation, choose trace sampling points, and run small hypothesis-driven trace experiments that feed directly into dashboard templates. This is intentionally lightweight — the goal is a repeatable rubric + experiment log that engineers and SREs can run during rollouts and model/onboarding work.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Use the Decision Rubric below to decide whether to add a metric, trace anchor, or dashboard tile.
- Prefer short iterative trace experiments (1–3 days) that produce a concrete action: change sampling, add a probe, or retire a panel.
- When in doubt, run a low-cost sampling experiment first (adaptive sampling at 0.1% -> 1% -> 5%) and collect representative spans tied to tenant/call attributes.

Decision Rubric (one-page):
1) What is the user-facing symptom or risk? (latency spike, increased 5xx, hallucination/regression)
2) How often does it occur? (singleton incident, daily, bursty)
3) What is the expected cost of missing it? (customer SLA violation, data leakage, no visible impact)
4) Can existing signals be composed to answer the hypothesis? (synthetic probes, kv-warmth, batch-size distribution)
5) If not, is a metric (aggregated), a trace anchor (span-level), or a prompt-level annotation required?
6) Estimate telemetry cost (query cost + storage) for 30 days at the proposed sampling rate.
7) Recommended action: instrument metric / add trace probe / run short sampling experiment / skip.

Rubric examples (concrete):
- Symptom: sudden 95th latency increase for text.generate.
  - Frequency: persistent for 3h, affects multiple tenants.
  - Recommendation: add trace anchor at serving-runtime -> tokenizer -> kv-cache, sampling 1% initially, dashboard tile showing 50/95/99 quantiles by model-version and tenant-weight.
  - Cost estimate: sampling 1% ~ +$120/mo for trace ingestion on high-throughput tenants.

- Symptom: model quality regression in rerank tests (internal evals).
  - Frequency: nightly regression run detects change in top-1 accuracy.
  - Recommendation: record prompt-level metadata and function-call spans for reranker, store small prompt hash and candidate embeddings for cheap diffs; dashboard: regression heatmap across prompt sets.

Trace Experiment Notebook (format to use for each experiment):
- Experiment id: YYYYMMDD-short-name (e.g., 20260115-kv-eviction-sample)
- Owner: name + pager/contact
- Hypothesis: one-line (what we think is happening)
- Signals to collect: (metric names, span names, attributes)
- Sampling plan: initial rate, escalation plan, retention window
- Duration: suggested 48–72h for production validation
- Success criteria: measurable threshold (e.g., root cause narrowed to eviction vs network; variance reduction in latency attribution)
- Actions on success / failure: add permanent anchor / increase sampling / close experiment

Sample experiment entry (realistic):
- Experiment id: 20260203-prefix-cold-cache-anchors
- Owner: Jordan Kim (oncall: eng-sre rotation)
- Hypothesis: Tenant-level prefix cold starts are driving 99p latency during morning ramp for small nightly-batch jobs.
- Signals to collect: request.latency_ms, kv.cache.hit_rate, span.kv.eviction (custom), tenant_id, sequence_length_bucket, model_version
- Sampling plan: start 0.25% sampling of full traces for 72h; escalate to 1% for 6h window during daily ramp if signal persists. Retain traces for 14 days.
- Duration: 72h baseline + optional escalation window
- Success criteria: observed correlation coefficient > 0.45 between low kv.hit_rate and 99p latency across tenants; identification of top 3 tenants for mitigation
- Actions: if success -> add permanent lightweight span anchor for kv.eviction and create per-tenant warming task; if fail -> broaden to additional spans (tokenizer, device-queue-wait)

Dashboard Template snippets (to paste into PRs):
- Panel: Latency Distribution by Tenant
  - Metric: request.latency_ms percentiles 50/95/99
  - Breakdowns: model_version, tenant_id (top N), kv_warmth_bucket
  - Alert: 99p > baseline*1.3 for 15m
- Panel: KV Warmth & Eviction Rate
  - Metric: kv.cache.hit_rate, kv.evictions_per_minute
  - Correlate with 99p latency via correlation scatter plot widget
- Panel: Trace Sampling Health
  - Metric: sampled_traces.count, sampled_traces.size_bytes, sampling_rate_over_time
  - Use to detect telemetry storms caused by experiment escalations

Telemetry cost heuristics (quick):
- Full traces are expensive: prefer span anchors (compact span + attributes) for long-term collection.
- Use adaptive sampling windows timed to traffic ramps to reduce baseline cost.
- For spike investigation: temporarily raise sampling + shorten retention, export heap of raw traces to GCS for offline deep-dive.

Operational playbook (short):
- Before rollout (model or infra): run a 24h synthetic probe that exercises key codepaths (small, medium, large prompts). Compare baseline percentiles.
- If rollout causes >10% increase in 95p latency for >30m, trigger trace experiment at 1% sampling anchored to the new model version and route to eng-sre + owning product eng.
- Postmortem: include experiment notebook entry and decision point (keep/rollback/mitigate).

Open questions / TODOs (for team):
- How to compress span metadata (remove PHI/prompt text) while preserving debugability? (Sofia to prototype redaction shim)
- Should we standardize a 6-field trace-anchor schema for inference flows? (proposal needed)
- Cost allocation: can we charge experiments to a temporary 'experiments' billing tag rather than tenant chargebacks? (Liam to consult finance)

Links & references:
- Quick checklist of related Playbooks: CONFLUENCE-obs/incident-telemetry-checklist, CONFLUENCE-obs/kvcache-instrumentation
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/87 (kv-cache span anchor schema)
- Slack threads: #obs-kv-evictions, #serving-runtime-incidents (referenced in JIRA-OBS-3421)

Action items (next steps):
- [ ] Maya: draft 6-field trace-anchor schema by 2026-03-01
- [ ] Jordan: spin a small sampling experiment for rerank-regressions using the above experiment template (id 20260210-rerank-sample)
- [ ] Liam: confirm billing approach with finance by 2026-02-28

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep experiments short and measurable. Avoid adding permanent panels until the signal is well-understood.
- When adding trace anchors, prefer attributes over full prompt recording; use prompt hashes + sampled snippet.
- Document every experiment as an entry in this doc and push summary to the rollout PR so reviewers see telemetry impact.

Revision log:
- 2025-11-10: initial draft (Jordan)
- 2026-01-18: added rubric examples and cost heuristics (Maya)
- 2026-02-25: appended experiment entries + action items (Liam)

End of notebook.
